questions.q: In Scenario 1, why did the new AP Specialist never get her job role provisioned?
options: She never clicked the self-request button
Her job field had a trailing space that didn't exactly match the role mapping's conditions, so autoprovisioning never fired
Autoprovisioning is disabled for all new hires at Castellan Robotics
Her manager rejected the approval request
questions.explain: A mismatch between the worker's job field and the role mapping's conditions (a trailing space) prevented autoprovisioning from triggering.

questions.q: In Scenario 2, what was the actual root cause of the Senior Accountant seeing fewer invoices than expected?
options: He had never been given any job role at all
The Invoices page was broken for all users
His password had expired
One of his two roles still had a stale, narrower business unit value that was never updated when he took on EMEA Shared Services
questions.explain: The business unit assignment was inconsistent across his two roles — one role was updated, the other still pointed to an old, narrower value.

questions.q: In Scenario 3, why did the regional controller's GL numbers look wrong even though her data access set was confirmed correct?
options: Because a balancing segment value had never been assigned a default ledger set during enterprise structure setup — a configuration gap, not a security problem
Because the problem was actually a security issue after all
Because her role was accidentally deleted
Because General Ledger does not support balancing segments
questions.explain: This scenario illustrates the Lesson 17 warning that not every 'wrong data' complaint is a security issue — this one was an enterprise structure setup gap.

questions.q: In Scenario 4, what was the correct response to the AP Supervisor's recurring access gaps, instead of granting him the full Accounts Payable Manager role?
options: Grant the full AP Manager role immediately, since it was the fastest fix
Deny all further access requests from him
Identify the one specific duty role he actually needed (adjusting supplier payment terms) and grant access to just that
Remove his existing Accounts Payable Supervisor role entirely
questions.explain: Granting the full AP Manager role would have given him unrequested payment-approval and policy-setting access — a segregation-of-duties risk avoided by identifying and granting only the specific missing duty role.

questions.q: What common theme runs through all four scenarios in this lesson?
options: Every access problem is ultimately caused by a weak password
Splitting function security from data security first, tracing the specific gap, and avoiding over-broad fixes
All problems were solved by granting every available job role
None of the scenarios required any investigation at all
questions.explain: Each scenario reinforces the Lesson 17 method: diagnose the specific cause using the function/data security split, and resist blanket over-provisioning as a shortcut.
